newsitem.title: INDIA: Power begins flowing again in northern India.
newsitem.headline: Power begins flowing again in northern India.

text.p: Indian power authorities began restoring electricity to the north on Friday after a breakdown blacked out the capital and several nearby states for most of the day.

"It is improving. We are in the process of restoration of the grid," said R.B. Mishra, a senior official with the state-run Power Grid, told Reuters. He said power had been restored to 70 percent of the capital New Delhi.
"In other states like Punjab, the situation has been revived," Mishra said.
Dozens of trains ground to halt across northern India soon after the early morning failure, the Press Trust of India reported.
A breakdown of the northern electricity grid left New Delhi as well as much of Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and Punjab states without power.
Uttar Pradesh, home to 140 million people, covers a large section of northern India.
PTI quoted Delhi Chief Minister Sahib Singh Verma as blaming the failure on Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan drawing more than their share of power from the grid.
